Worrell, E., Blinde, P., Neelis, M., Blomen, E. and Masanet, E. (2010). Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the U.S. Iron and Steel Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers. Report LBNL-4779E, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, October 2010. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 10). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue: almost every number is reprinted from other sources. Main file (22 technologies): Table 4-1 process-step energy use (IISI 1998) for sinter, coke, hot stoves, blast furnace, BOF, EAF, continuous casting, reheating furnace and hot strip mill, loaded as final fuel (target fuel) and electricity with the printed average as value and the printed range as min/max, converted from per-short-ton units with an explicit formula; whole technologies with their own energy or cost figures: BOF with gas recovery (net -0.30 GJ/t), ladle preheating (BOF and caster), combustion and induction tundish heating (efficiency), strip caster, typical EAF (441 kWh/t), Consteel and DC EAF, continuous annealing line (capex $225 million for 450,000 t/yr, fuel with and without heat recovery), heat-recovery coke ovens (capacity), steel-mill boilers (55-85%), low-calorific-gas turbine (33% net, LHV) and the micro back-pressure let-down turbine ($600/kWe, $0.011/kWh). Flows: blast furnace gas export 5 GJ/t pig iron. _measures.csv: all quantified measures of Chapters 9-21 (cross-cutting and process-specific) with saving, cost and payback as printed. _other-values.csv: Table 4-1 net primary energy, chapter-text restatements of the IISI best-practice averages in GJ/tonne (not loaded, to avoid duplicating Table 4-1), theoretical minima, gas yields and heating values, capacities and sector statistics. Not loaded: water-efficiency measures (Chapter 23), qualitative Chapter 22 technologies (TGR-BF, HIsarna, electrolysis, CCS), sector statistics and figures read only from charts.

(1) Table 4-1 values are reprinted from IISI (1998) and are per short ton; Sinter electricity range printed reversed ('28-20'); Coke primary energy has no average; Hot strip mill fuel has only a single value. (2) BOF net primary energy is positive in Table 4-1 (0.06-0.5 MBtu/ton, avg 0.3) but Chapter 18 reports an energy surplus of 0.26 MBtu/ton (0.30 GJ/tonne) for the same IISI source (the latter includes gas recovery). (3) Chapter text converts 1.5 MBtu/ton to 1.8 GJ/tonne and 1.1 to 1.2 GJ/tonne, inconsistent with footnote 7 factor 1.16 (1.74 and 1.28). (4) DC arc furnace power 500-600 kWh/tonne is higher than the typical AC figure (441 kWh/tonne) although DC is said to save about 5%. (5) No price year or cost basis for any cost (continuous annealing $225 million, expansion turbine $600/kWe, measure costs). (6) Heating-value basis not stated for energy intensities (only BF gas and the LCV gas turbine are given as LHV). (7) Voltage-unbalance saving printed without unit ('savings of 9,500'). (8) Text fragments with unresolved edits: 'in what year?' (p.17, p.24), 'Figure 4-711-2' (p.53), 'IISI' vs 'IPPC' citation mix-ups; 'blast oxygen furnace' for basic oxygen furnace (p.86); '3.25 Nm3 per tonne of coal' contradicts 360 Nm3/t (p.11); 'North Star Steel ... 140 TBtu (148 TJ)' unit slip (p.34). (9) Chapter 7 describes chapters 6-11/12/13-19 with numbering that does not match the actual chapters 8-21.
